name: Deep speech-in-speech hiding
definition: Encoder-decoder networks with differentiable spectral transforms hide speech in speech.

name: Balanced partition
definition: The cover alphabet is split into two near-equiprobable halves and a key bit picks the half to sample from.

name: Capacity laws
definition: Results on how much can be hidden securely as the amount of cover grows; secure capacity scales with the square root of cover size.

name: Complexity-theoretic security
definition: Security is computational indistinguishability of stegotext from the channel.

name: Constructions with stated security
definition: Concrete stegosystems built to meet one of the security models.

name: Informal limits and terminology
definition: A survey-level account of attacks and of why no Shannon-style theory of steganography yet exists.

name: Information-theoretic security
definition: Detection is a hypothesis test and security is the relative entropy between cover and stego distributions.

name: Keyed function of a robust feature
definition: A keyed function of a feature that survives editing (a document's maximising shingle) carries the bit.

name: Keyed parity embedding
definition: A key selects a set of cover elements and each bit is embedded as their parity.

name: Public-key steganography
definition: The message is encrypted under the recipient's public key and embedded as the parity of successive cover blocks.

name: Rejection sampling
definition: Channel samples are drawn repeatedly until a keyed or unbiased function of the sample equals the next message bit.

name: Security models
definition: Formal or informal definitions of what it means for a stegosystem to be undetectable.

name: Shared-sample robust code
definition: Channel draws made with pseudorandom inputs both parties share stand in for shared blocks, so that the message survives bounded changes by an active warden.

name: Subliminal channels
definition: A choice among several valid cryptographic outputs that all authenticate the same message carries a hidden message.

name: Uniform-cover schemes
definition: When covers are uniformly distributed, a key-shifted choice among them is perfectly secure.

name: Universal-compression stegosystems
definition: A universal compressor approximates the unknown cover distribution, and its decompressor generates stegotext.

name: Real-time action commands
definition: Bits are carried by player commands in a real-time game, such as which units are selected, through a combinatorial selection scheme.

name: Chess-data codebook
definition: Message symbols are mapped to chess content (squares, pieces, players) written in chess-related text.

name: Comment codebook
definition: Synonymous annotation comments each stand for a bit pattern.

name: Outcome-equivalent moves
definition: A keyed generator chooses among moves that lead to the same outcome.

name: Keyed strategy-set coding
definition: The set of best moves is permuted by a shared random number generator and seed, and message bits index into the permuted set.

name: Learned action policies
definition: Each message symbol has its own trained policy and the receiver decodes by recognising which policy produced the actions.

name: Mixed-radix legal-move encoding
definition: Ciphertext read as an integer is written digit by digit as choices among all legal moves, each position supplying its own radix.
notes: Ignores move quality, so the game need not look plausible.

name: Move-choice channels
definition: The message decides which legal move or action is played.

name: Move-choice indexing
definition: A prearranged criterion orders a set of acceptable moves, and the index of the move played sends that value.

name: Ranked-move index
definition: A shared engine lists acceptable moves in order and the index of the move played carries bits.

name: Game-record and annotation channels
definition: The message sits in material around the moves: comments, inserted variations or chess data in text.

name: Physical and acoustic side signals
definition: Players signal hidden information through an agreed physical act outside the game moves, such as card orientation or a sound.

name: Inserted variations
definition: Bits are carried by where a variation starts in an already played game, its length and its moves.

name: Hyperbolic-space hiding
definition: Message and carrier features are blended in a Poincare ball rather than in Euclidean space.

name: Adversarially adjusted costs
definition: Embedding costs are made asymmetric by the gradient of a target steganalyser so the stego image also fools it.

name: Distortion-minimising embedding
definition: Embedding assigns costs to modifications of image elements and works under the framework of minimising total distortion.

name: Adversarially trained hiding
definition: A steganalyser or discriminator is trained in the loop against the encoder.

name: Cover-dependent deep hiding
definition: The hiding network sees both cover and secret, with or without a preparation network.

name: Learned encoder-decoder hiding
definition: An encoder network takes the cover image and the message and outputs a residual that is added back to the image; a decoder network recovers the message.

name: Physical-channel hiding
definition: Training simulates printing, display and camera capture so the message survives a physical channel.

name: Universal deep hiding
definition: The secret is encoded independently of the cover and the same perturbation can be added to any cover.

name: Attribute mapping (cover selection)
definition: Unmodified natural images are chosen because their own attributes map to the message under an agreed rule.

name: Diffusion inversion translation
definition: A diffusion model inverts a secret image and regenerates it under another condition as the container, and the receiver inverts back.

name: Generative synthesis
definition: A shared generator produces the container image directly from the message, so no cover is modified.

name: Grille and inpainting
definition: The message is written at positions marked by a shared mask and a generator inpaints the rest of the image.

name: Image-hash mapping
definition: A hash of low-level features (grey values, HOG, SIFT, DCT, deep features, file attributes) is matched to message segments through an index.

name: Message-to-latent mapping
definition: Message bits are mapped to the generator's input noise and a trained extractor recovers them from the image.

name: Latent search
definition: The generator's latent space is searched for a code whose output carries the message.

name: Generator-model database
definition: A database of generator models turns a secret image into an unrelated-looking image and back.

name: Partial-duplicate patch retrieval
definition: Patches of a secret image are matched by retrieved natural images and stitched back at the receiver.

name: Secret-conditioned generator
definition: A module inside the generator writes the secret into its feature maps during image generation.

name: Visual-word mapping
definition: Visual words found in images are mapped to text keywords so selected images express a text message.

name: Agentic stegosystem construction
definition: A tool-using agent must build a working stegosystem from a provided paper, not merely describe one.

name: Codeword substitution
definition: Agreed codewords stand in for the hidden states.

name: Control evaluations
definition: A blue team's protocol of trusted and untrusted models is scored by a red team's best attack, including collusion.

name: Coordination-without-communication evaluations
definition: Models must coordinate with copies of themselves with no shared channel or memory.

name: Prompted encoded reasoning
definition: Models carry out hidden reasoning in an encoded form inside visible text.

name: Evaluation frameworks and decompositions
definition: Frameworks that organise or split capability measurement (by capability or by role) rather than test one scheme.

name: Encoded message passing
definition: An encoder hides a secret in its answer to a cover task for a decoder copy, and a monitor without the secret judges suspicion.

name: Overt encodings as capabilities
definition: Standard encodings and ciphers are tested as a measure of whether models can encode and decode at all.

name: Graded partial encoding
definition: A cipher is applied to each word with a set probability, interpolating between legible and fully enciphered text.

name: Prompted elicitation
definition: Models are prompted to act as encoder and decoder against a monitor, without any training on the task.

name: Codes learned under RL pressure
definition: Reinforcement learning against penalised strings leads models to learn substitute encodings, which tend to rest on semantic links to the penalised strings.

name: Scheme-discovery condition
definition: The model is asked to think of a scheme for the task, use it, and later re-derive it to decode; what it devises is not fixed.
notes: Replaces lgt-model-devised; the schemes found are placed by mechanism.

name: Stateless protocol subversion
definition: A model must devise and act on a plan to subvert a control protocol across contexts with no shared memory.

name: Taught schemes
definition: A given scheme is instilled by fine-tuning, RL or in-context examples, and the study measures whether the model can use it.

name: Training-induced steganography
definition: Fine-tuning or reinforcement learning is used to induce or teach hidden encoding.

name: Fixed bins
definition: A shared random partition of the vocabulary into equal bins lets each token's bin carry a fixed number of bits.

name: Byte encodings
definition: The message is written as Base64, hexadecimal or binary strings.

name: Count and state-tracking codes
definition: A state is carried by first letters, word or character counts modulo the number of states, or similar countable features.

name: Coupling-based codes
definition: Uniform-looking ciphertext is joined to the covertext distribution by a coupling, so the published token is drawn exactly from the cover distribution.

name: Maximal coupling through a public draft model
definition: A small public draft model run by both parties partitions the vocabulary and a maximal coupling samples the token from the sender's private distribution.

name: Distribution copies
definition: Rotated copies of the token distribution are built at each step and the message chooses which copy to sample from.

name: Entity and keyword mapping
definition: Message bits index entries in a shared entity tree or keyword set, which the LLM is prompted to mention and the receiver reads back.

name: Enumerated openers
definition: The message selects one of a fixed list of openings or stated values with which the answer begins.

name: Feedback (posterior-matching) coding
definition: Each generated token is seen by both parties and guides the next embedding step, as in coding over a channel with noiseless feedback.
notes: The paper calls its setting black-box; access_needed now gives sender and receiver separately.

name: Encoders trained into the weights
definition: A model is fine-tuned so that it writes a secret from its prompt into ordinary completions, with the code held in its weights rather than in a sampling rule.

name: Probability grouping
definition: The vocabulary is split into groups of near-equal probability and the message chooses a group, recursively, before a token is sampled within it.

name: Per-step Huffman codes
definition: A Huffman code is rebuilt from the model's distribution at every step and the message bits walk the code tree to a token.

name: Thresholded (patient) Huffman
definition: The Huffman code is used only at steps where its distance from the model's distribution is below a threshold; other steps sample normally.

name: Initial-class codes
definition: The class of a token's initial letter (A-M against N-Z) carries a bit, rather than the letter itself.
notes: Unprescribed: models adopted it although the rules did not assign it.

name: Interval coding with per-step truncation
definition: The number of candidate tokens kept at each step is chosen adaptively so the truncated distribution stays within a divergence bound of the model's.

name: Interval (arithmetic) coding
definition: The message is read as a point in the unit interval and decoded into tokens by arithmetic coding run in reverse over the model's distributions.

name: Keyed sampling-randomness embedding
definition: Pseudorandomly masked message bits stand in for the sampling random number, and the bits consumed per token follow the token's entropy.
notes: Meteor; the cryptographic, stateful successor to plain interval coding.

name: Letter-position codes (acrostics)
definition: Message letters are placed at agreed positions, such as the first letters of sentences or words.

name: Literal payload as a name
definition: The payload is written directly into the text as an imagined acronym or name.

name: Overt encodings and ciphers
definition: The message is transformed by a standard encoding or cipher and written into the text, hiding its content but not its presence.
notes: Not steganography in the strict sense; kept because evaluations use them as baselines.

name: Prompted pre-agreed rule codes
definition: The model is told an explicit encoding rule and applies it while writing; the receiver applies the inverse rule.

name: Keyless key exchange in samples
definition: Public-key (lattice) ciphertext is carried in sampled text so two parties with no shared secret can agree a key covertly.

name: Reasoning-strategy choice
definition: Each reasoning step carries a bit by realising or omitting an agreed reasoning strategy.

name: Distribution-preserving sampling codes
definition: The message replaces or steers the randomness used to sample each token from a shared language model, so the stegotext follows the model's own distribution.
notes: Access differs by child: Meteor needs the distribution at both ends, BAM (guo_2026) needs none at the receiver, and Codetta (pang_2026) needs only a public draft model there.

name: Black-box semantic-choice schemes
definition: The message picks the keywords a generated sentence is built around (subject, predicate, object, emotion), and an LLM reached through prompts writes the sentence.

name: Substitution ciphers
definition: Each letter of the message is replaced by another under a fixed mapping.

name: Surface-formatting codes
definition: Bits are carried by formatting choices such as capitalisation, markdown, whitespace runs or interjections.

name: Free task-choice codes
definition: The repetitive, supposedly arbitrary choices a task leaves open, such as variable names or items chosen, carry the information.

name: Bin and Huffman codes
definition: The vocabulary is divided into shared disjoint bins, or another shared code over it, and the token chosen at each step carries a block of message bits.

name: Watermark-derived multi-bit codes
definition: A language-model watermark is extended to carry a message, which a keyed detector recovers from the generated text.

name: Pseudorandom undetectable watermark codes
definition: Keyed pseudorandom sampling makes the watermark, and so the payload, computationally undetectable without the key.

name: Token-partition (red-green) watermark codes
definition: The message seeds or selects a partition of tokens into favoured and disfavoured sets, and the decoder picks the message whose partition scores highest.
notes: Biases the distribution, so not distribution-preserving.

name: Markov-model generation with range partition
definition: A message read as a number selects successive words from a Markov text model by probability-proportional ranges.
notes: Pre-neural ancestor of lgt-interval-coding; the same mechanism (m-interval-plain) in the mechanism tree.

name: Authenticate, then throw games
definition: Colluders identify one another through a keyed signal and then lose deliberately to a designated winner.

name: Collusion audits and taxonomies
definition: Frameworks, benchmarks and detectors that measure or classify collusion rather than perform it.

name: Collusion benchmarks
definition: Scenario suites in which collusion can occur are scored by outcome measures such as coalition regret or detection.

name: Natural-language covertext codebooks
definition: Agents hide a message in ordinary-looking text through word choice or topic, using a codebook or knowledge the overseer lacks.

name: Emergent codes in interaction
definition: Meaning arises in an unprescribed channel (numbers, symbols, compressed text) through repeated interaction.

name: Focality prompts
definition: The prompt tells the model what kind of salience to aim at (cultural, perceptual or a list of focality principles).

name: Gradient-based RL
definition: The sender's weights are updated by RL to maximise the receiver's success minus an overseer's suspicion.

name: In-context RL
definition: An LLM learner revises natural-language strategies between episodes while the weights stay fixed.

name: Input triggers
definition: Both colluders misbehave only when an agreed feature is present in the input, so no message passes between them.

name: Codes learned by optimisation
definition: The sender and receiver discover their scheme by optimisation against task reward and an overseer, rather than being given it.

name: Learned tacit collusion
definition: Learning agents drift into collusive strategies through interaction alone, with no message and no plan to collude.

name: Output signals
definition: The sender puts an agreed mark in its own output, such as a variable name, so the receiver knows to act.

name: Pre-agreed codes and signals
definition: Colluders fix a code or signal in advance and use it to recognise each other or to pass a message.

name: Risk taxonomies
definition: Multi-agent failures are sorted into modes and risk factors.

name: Prompted Schelling coordination
definition: Isolated copies of a model independently choose the same scheme, signal or parameters because the choice is salient to both.

name: Tacit coordination
definition: Agents coordinate without exchanging a message, by converging on the same choice.

name: Collusion trigger signals
definition: An agreed feature of the input or the output tells a colluding monitor when to look away; often a single bit.

name: Symmetry-robust conventions
definition: Training against relabelled copies of a partner removes arbitrary conventions so that agents coordinate with partners they have not met.
notes: A method for coordination rather than collusion; included as the learning analogue of focal points.

name: Chess language and commentary
definition: Models and data that join chess positions and natural-language text.

name: Chess language models and datasets
definition: Language models and contrastive models trained on games paired with chess text.

name: Commentary evaluation
definition: LLM judges, given engine input, score commentary quality.

name: Commentary generation
definition: Systems that write commentary on moves from engine and game features.

name: Engine and opening-tree analysis
definition: Engines and game databases are used to measure opening breadth, popularity or variant balance.

name: Engine-benchmarked skill assessment
definition: A player's moves are compared with an engine's choices, for example as the percentage that match, to measure skill or detect cheating.

name: Models of human move choice
definition: Statistical or neural models of which move a human of given strength plays; candidate cover distributions or warden models for move-choice channels.

name: Hyperbolic embeddings and measurement
definition: Methods that place data or model states in hyperbolic space, or measure how hyperbolic they are.

name: Hyperbolic network layers and agents
definition: Neural layers, adapters and RL agents that compute in hyperbolic space.

name: Intrinsic rating models
definition: Engine evaluations of the reasonable moves give each a probability, fitted to players' skill.

name: LLM chess play
definition: Benchmarks that measure how well language models play chess, with no hidden message.

name: Neural human-move predictors
definition: Networks trained on human games predict the human move or mistake at a given rating.

name: Activation probes
definition: Linear or small probes on hidden states read deception or reconstruct the secret.

name: Active-warden defences
definition: The overseer rewrites, redacts or paraphrases messages to destroy any hidden payload instead of only detecting it.

name: Concept-lens readout and intervention
definition: Concepts read through a Jacobian lens are compared across agents or swapped to test causal use.

name: Game-record inference
definition: Complete game records are analysed for actions too good for the information the player legitimately had.

name: Game-statistics attacks
definition: Game length, playing level and result are tested against games without hidden data.

name: Internal-state detection
definition: Hidden communication is detected from model activations rather than from the text.

name: Likelihood-ratio forensics
definition: The hypothesis that players used a specified method to transmit information is weighed against the hypothesis that they did not.

name: LLM-based classifiers
definition: A fine-tuned LLM judges whether a text carries hidden data.

name: Prompted LLM monitors
definition: A model given the cover task and answer, but not the secret, rates suspicion, and a threshold set at a fixed false-positive rate decides.

name: Statistical and feature steganalysis
definition: A detector compares measured features of suspect objects with those of covers.

name: Text feature steganalysis
definition: Hand-built features of word choice, such as synonym context fitness, feed a classifier.

name: Decision-theoretic utility gap
definition: Steganography is detected by the gap in downstream usefulness of a message to a party who can decode it and one who cannot.

name: Fine-tuned decoder
definition: The latent decoder is fine-tuned so all generated images carry a fixed signature.

name: Watermarks in the generator
definition: The generative model is altered so that every output carries the mark.

name: Initial-noise pattern
definition: A key is written into the initial noise of a diffusion model and detected after inversion.

name: Learned post-hoc watermarks
definition: A trained network adds a robust mark to existing media (audio, image or text).
